learn.title: Parallel lines
learn.body: Parallel lines run side by side and never meet. They have the same slope. The lines $y=2x+1$ and $y=2x-5$ are parallel, since both have slope 2.

learn.title: Perpendicular lines
learn.body: Perpendicular lines meet at a right angle. Their slopes are negative reciprocals: flip the fraction and change the sign. Slope 2 goes with $-\frac{1}{2}$, and their product is $-1$.

learn.title: Parallel through a point
learn.body: Find the line parallel to $y=2x+1$ through $(1,4)$.

learn.title: Perpendicular through a point
learn.body: Find the line perpendicular to $y=2x+1$ through $(4,1)$.
Put both lines in $y=mx+b$ form before comparing slopes. Standard form hides the slope.

questions.prompt: What is the slope of any line parallel to $y=3x-1$?
questions.explanation: Parallel lines have the same slope, so they never meet.

questions.prompt: What slope is perpendicular to a line of slope 2? Give a fraction.
questions.explanation: Flip 2 to $\frac{1}{2}$ and change the sign: $-\frac{1}{2}$.

questions.prompt: What slope is perpendicular to $-\frac{3}{4}$? Give a fraction.
questions.explanation: Flip to $\frac{4}{3}$ and change the sign. $-\frac{3}{4}$ was negative, so the answer is positive.
Equal slopes mean equal steepness, so the lines never cross.

questions.prompt: Which pair of lines is parallel?
questions.explanation: Only the first pair has equal slopes (both 2).

questions.prompt: Match each line with the slope of a perpendicular line.
questions.explanation: Take the reciprocal and change the sign.

questions.prompt: A line is parallel to $y=2x+1$ and passes through $(1,4)$. What is its $y$-intercept?
A line is perpendicular to $y=2x+1$ and passes through $(4,1)$. What is its $y$-intercept?
Are $y=2x+3$ and $x+2y=8$ parallel, perpendicular or neither?
questions.explanation: $x+2y=8$ gives $y=-\frac{1}{2}x+4$. The slopes are $2$ and $-\frac{1}{2}$, and their product is $-1$.
